passage: On May 16th, 2001, a document called The HipHop Declaration of Peace was handed to the United Nations.
By accepting it, the world formally treated hip-hop as an international culture of peace.
The declaration also called attention to the genre's first purpose, which was to calm the violence of the Bronx.
In this way it showed that hip-hop's history had earned worldwide respect.
A second milestone arrived in 2018, when the rapper Kendrick Lamar received a Pulitzer Prize for Music.
That award placed a music once confined to the underground beside forms as established as classical composition.
Today listeners treat hip-hop as a way to speak for themselves, to resist unfairness, and to press for social change.
Because that appeal keeps widening, hip-hop remains a phenomenon on a global scale.
choices: hip-hop's growth into a globally recognized art form and voice for change
the procedures by which the United Nations approves cultural documents
the reasons classical music continues to dominate serious concert halls
the history of gang violence in the Bronx during the 1970s
the difficulty of judging popular music by traditional artistic standards
theme.explanation_ko: UN 선언문과 퓰리처상, 그리고 오늘날의 쓰임이 모두 힙합의 세계적 인정과 사회적 역할로 수렴하므로 ①이 주제이다.
theme.distractor_ko: ② UN의 승인 절차는 설명되지 않는다. ③ 클래식의 우위는 본문과 반대이다. ④ 브롱크스는 본래의 사명을 말하는 배경으로만 언급된다. ⑤ 심사 기준의 어려움은 다루지 않는다.
